Lesson 02: Exploring How Plants Respond to Light (Grade 3, Explore Phase, 5E Model)

Learning Objective: Students will investigate and describe how plants respond to changes in light
direction (phototropism).

Performance Expectation: 3-LS1-1. Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse
life cycles but all have in common birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
DCI: LS1.B — Growth and Development of Organisms
Focal SEP: Planning and Carrying Out Investigations
Focal CCC: Cause and Effect

Timing: 45 minutes

Student-Facing Sequence:
1. Hook (5 min): Students observe two potted seedlings, one grown near a window and one grown in a
   dark closet, and record initial observations in their science notebook.
2. Investigation Setup (10 min): In small groups, students set up a simple phototropism investigation
   using bean seedlings and a one-sided light source, predicting what will happen over the next week.
3. Data Collection Introduction (10 min): Teacher models how to measure stem angle with a protractor
   and record it in a data table. Students practice on a sample seedling.
4. Small-Group Investigation (15 min): Students measure and record the current stem angle of their own
   seedling, then place it in the light box.
5. Wrap-Up Discussion (5 min): Whole-class discussion: "What do you think will happen to the stem
   over the next few days, and why?" Students share predictions verbally with a partner.

Teacher Notes: Circulate to check students are using the protractor correctly. Sample response for
wrap-up: "I think the stem will bend toward the light because the plant needs light to make food."

Vocabulary: phototropism, stimulus, response, stem angle.

Assessment Opportunity: Notebook entry with initial observation drawing and predicted outcome.

Existing Literacy Supports: A vocabulary box with picture cards for "phototropism" and "stimulus" is
provided on the classroom word wall. No structured writing scaffold is provided for the prediction.
